{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. The distribution shows right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81) and potential outliers; consider log-transformation or robust ANOVA. If variance heterogeneity is severe, Welch's ANOVA alternative.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) violates ANOVA normality assumption. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence, or Cochran's Q if repeated measures structure exists. ANOVA inappropriate.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Extreme right skew (max=29.82, mean=0.47) and heavy tail suggest log-transformation or non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test as primary analysis. Check for zero/near-zero values before transformation.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Moderate right skew (max=75.35, mean=12.50) but less extreme than other variables; ANOVA may be reasonable with robust standard errors or bootstrap. Verify homogeneity of variance.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] with mean=0.38, sd=0.24; beta regression or arcsine-square-root transformation may improve model fit. Standard ANOVA acceptable if diagnostics pass."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures from 8 mice (n=76655 total, 8 mice). Standard ANOVA assumes independence; mixed-effects models with Mouse as random effect required for valid inference.",
    "Normality: QQ plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals; severe violations expected for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and Success.",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Levene's test; likely violated given disparate ranges across paradigms.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined paradigm dominates (48,846/76,655 = 63.7%), creating power imbalances in pairwise comparisons.",
    "Outliers: Winsorization or robust methods needed given extreme maxima in Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and Average Speed."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant: Tukey HSD for pairwise comparisons with family-wise error control, or Holm-Bonferroni correction for unequal sample sizes.",
    "For Success (logistic regression): Estimated marginal means with Tukey adjustment on log-odds scale, back-transformed to probability differences.",
    "For non-parametric alternatives (Kruskal-Wallis): Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction for pairwise comparisons.",
    "Focus comparisons: Combined vs each unimodal condition (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and vs Sham; plus unimodal vs Sham to assess baseline effects.",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d for continuous variables (with correction for unequal n), odds ratios for Success, Cliff's delta for non-parametric comparisons."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows fastest Time-to-Target and highest Success rate given largest sample size and presumed design as optimal condition.",
    "ICMS Only and visual conditions may show intermediate performance between Combined and Sham.",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance (longest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, lowest Path Efficiency).",
    "Path Efficiency and AD may discriminate multimodal integration effects: Combined may show highest Path Efficiency and lowest AD (more direct paths).",
    "Average Speed may show smaller paradigm effects if speed-accuracy trade-offs are balanced."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe sample size imbalance (Combined 63.7% of data) reduces power for detecting differences among smaller groups, especially Bright Visual Only (n=3,323, 4.3%).",
    "Repeated measures structure ignored in standard ANOVA; Mouse-level clustering inflates Type I error if not modeled.",
    "No information on trial-level covariates (learning effects, session effects, difficulty levels) that may confound paradigm comparisons.",
    "Extreme outliers and heavy tails in multiple variables threaten validity of parametric tests; robustness checks essential.",
    "Success as binary outcome makes ANOVA inappropriate; alternative analyses required.",
    "Single replication (Run 2) with temperature=0.25; no assessment of LLM response stability across replications or temperatures."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for continuous outcomes and generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) for Success, with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect. Include session/trial covariates if available. Use robust regression (MM-estimators) or quantile regression for Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target due to heavy tails. Conduct equivalence tests (TOST) for non-significant pairwise comparisons to distinguish null effects from underpowered tests. Validate findings with permutation-based inference given distributional concerns."
}
